name: New York Department of State Licensee Search

agency.name: New York Department of State Division of Licensing Services

updateFrequency: unknown; the official page notes searches are limited to active licenses only
licenseTypesIncluded: New York Department of State active license records exposed by licensee search, including construction-adjacent Home Inspection licenses where available
knownExclusions: New York State does not license home improvement contractors through this DOS source; home-improvement contractor licensing is handled by listed cities and counties where required.
The DOS search is limited to active licenses and is not a complete historical license source.
Skilled trades, NYC Department of Buildings licenses, local home-improvement licenses, and county consumer-affairs records require separate source entries.
Home Inspection licenses are construction-adjacent professional credentials and must not be treated as contractor licenses.
rateLimitNotes: No adapter is implemented. Prefer official export options if discovered before lookup automation.
publicRecordsNotes: Official DOS active-license lookup metadata only. Absence from this source is not proof that a home-inspector license, contractor license, local authorization, or inactive/historical credential does not exist elsewhere.
officialBulkDownloadNotes: No official construction-specific bulk download has been confirmed in this phase.
researchNotes: Registry-only source for New York DOS licensee search. DOS Home Inspection licenses are construction-adjacent professional credentials; the board-coverage ledger treats statewide contractor and skilled-trade licensing separately.
maintainerNotes: Keep active-only, home-inspector-only, and local-contractor-licensing limitations prominent.

researchEvidence.note: Official DOS page reviewed; it lists searchable active license categories including Home Inspection and states that searches are limited to active licenses only.
Official DOS Home Inspector page reviewed; it defines home inspection as observing and reporting on residential building systems and components, with a two-year license term.
Official DOS consumer alert reviewed; it states that New York State does not license home improvement contractors and identifies local jurisdictions that do.

blocker.summary: No stable, documented machine-readable official interface is currently suitable for an offline-tested adapter.
